video_title: What Is Going On With Kawhi & The Clippers? Big Decisions For Denver & Phoenix

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs players and staff had better access to the Louvre than Windhorst
quotes.excerpt: The Spurs got a little bit better access to the Louvre than I did.
quotes.quote: The Spurs have all been over here all week, Victor Wembanyama hosting a get-together with most of the Spurs team. They've been around town. They got a little bit better access to the Louvre than I did. They posted a photo of all of them right next to the Mona Lisa in the room by themselves. I did not have such access.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA teams are subsidizing summer team trips by sending personnel
quotes.excerpt: I think the team sometimes secretly subsidizes it a little bit.
quotes.quote: It is definitely something that most teams do. I think the team sometimes secretly subsidizes it a little bit. They certainly subsidize it by sending personnel there in a lot of cases to make sure their players are taken care of. Last year we had the really unfortunate situation with Fred VanVleet when he tore his ACL on the Rockets trip to the Bahamas.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers built a new facility in the Intuit Dome
quotes.excerpt: The Clippers, they built a new facility in Intuit Dome.
quotes.quote: Some teams have gone to the Union's facility in Spain. The Union has a facility in Spain. In fact, the Union just announced this week that they officially opened it. The Clippers, they built a new facility in Intuit Dome. How about that for a transition I'm about to make? And their old facility in LA in Playa Vista, the Union acquired. And so now the Union has a base in New York.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA teams are getting new jets with lay-flat seats
quotes.excerpt: The first new NBA jet is ready. It just got delivered in the last week.
quotes.quote: Over the next year they're getting replaced and the first new NBA jet is ready. It just got delivered in the last week, I think it got delivered last week or so. And you know what the upgrade on this Slater is? Is that now they have lay-flat seats.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Kawhi Leonard allegedly had a secret sponsorship deal with Daktronics
quotes.excerpt: Kawhi Leonard had a hidden, multimillion-dollar sponsorship with Clippers' scoreboard-makers.
quotes.quote: Pablo Torre late last week had an update to his reporting on Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers. And let me just say, it involved the scoreboard-maker Daktronics, who did the $100 million scoreboard at Intuit Dome, the Halo board they called it. It's an unusual scoreboard like no one ever seen. Kawhi Leonard had a hidden, multimillion-dollar sponsorship with Clippers' scoreboard-makers, sources tell Pablo Torre. It was a way to circumvent the salary cap, insider says.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Windhorst questions the business model of Aspiration and carbon credits
quotes.excerpt: The guy who ran Aspiration was a fraudster.
quotes.quote: For me, Slater, it was hard to understand because I didn't understand what Aspiration was as a company. I didn't understand carbon credits. I mean, I understand the general concept of it, but I didn't understand how this was such a big business, planting trees and selling carbon credits. And the guy who ran Aspiration was a fraudster. The one thing that throughout the entire Aspiration scandal, and I am not an investigative reporter, nor am I doing, I did a little bit of reporting on that story, like I called some other Clippers sponsors and asked them if they were ever asked to throw money Kawhi's way and they said no. But from where I sat, the guy who went to prison for many years, this guy Joe Sandberg, to me it looked to me like it was a Ponzi scheme where he needed new investment to keep his Ponzi scheme going and he did whatever made Steve Ballmer happy because he was where he was getting the new investment from.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Dillon Brooks signs a three-year, $73 million extension with the Suns
quotes.excerpt: Dillon Brooks agreeing to a three-year, $73 million contract extension with the Phoenix Suns.
quotes.quote: Dillon Brooks agreeing to a three-year, $73 million contract extension with the Phoenix Suns through 2029-30. Mike George of Klutch Sports tells ESPN. Brooks has become a key part of the Suns two-way, hard-nosed culture under Jordan Ott and lands a new guaranteed long-term deal.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Suns expected to eventually extend Miles Bridges
quotes.excerpt: The expectation is that they're going to eventually extend Miles Bridges.
quotes.quote: The expectation is that they're going to eventually extend Miles Bridges. They traded for Miles Bridges this summer. We call Phoenix West Lansing. Bridges has one year, $23 million left on his contract. It doesn't appear he's going to extend this summer. He has to wait, I think he's got to wait six months. We could use Bobby Marks to help us with that, but it doesn't appear he's going to extend this summer.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Davis waiting until the season to sign an extension
quotes.excerpt: Anthony Davis is going to wait until the season.
quotes.quote: This is kind of like the Shams report the other day of Anthony Davis is going to wait until the season. Almost nobody wants to wait until the season. You typically want your deal done, but I think eventually there's a very good chance that Miles Bridges is going to get extended, is my point.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.excerpt: Don Nelson passed away, 86 years old. Many people are going to have many things to say.
quotes.quote: Don Nelson passed away, 86 years old. Many people are going to have many things to say. We're not going to say all of it here. I was supposed to have McMahon on this podcast, but I literally got the day wrong because McMahon is at a family event in the South Pacific and I told him that this podcast was happening on Monday morning, it was actually on Sunday morning. Don Nelson is a Hall of Famer and changed the game in many ways. And Slater, for the people in the Bay Area, the seeds of the Warriors dynasty were planted by Don Nelson. And Larry Riley and the other folks who started drafting those players. Don Nelson was a Hall of Famer. I remember one of my memories was right near the end of his coaching time with Golden State, when there was a game in Cleveland like in mid-December, mid-December, January, it was freezing outside and he held shootaround and I came to shootaround and I remember he had this plastic bag full of cigars. He had that in one hand and in the other hand he had a cigar holder with space for three cigars and he was looking through each cigar and smelling it and deciding and no that's no good, throwing it. He had like 10 in this plastic bag. He's like, oh that's a good one, put that in the holder. And he goes through a couple more, no, no, no. Okay, when he had three good ones and he closed off his cigar holder, he put it in his pocket and he turned around and he goes, bus is leaving.
